intro: Roofers coordinate with crews, work at height and race the weather. The closest of the 25 careers below is helping brick, stone and tile setters at an 84% match, but Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic are 73% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $63,870, or 15% more.
why_it_works: A roofing job means planning materials, working safely on steep surfaces and finishing before rain. O*NET rates coordination at 3.75 out of 5 for roofers, and time management and operation and control at 3. Mining, welding, layout and line work use the same physical and planning skills. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The gaps are equipment maintenance and troubleshooting.
tips: Power-line work is the best-paid close option: installers earn $95,320, which is 72% more.
Your comfort at height is an advantage for line, tower and wind turbine jobs.
Commercial Divers earn $72,990, or 32% more, after a certificate program.

faq.q: What jobs can former roofers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are helpers for brick, stone and tile setters (84%), roofer helpers (79%) and surface mining excavating operators (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Welders are 73% matched and earn $53,750, which is 3% less than the $55,440 roofer median.

faq.q: Which careers for roofers pay more?
faq.a: 11 of the 25 matches pay more. Power-line installers earn $95,320 (72% more), Locomotive Engineers $81,410 (47% more) and Commercial Divers $72,990 (32% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Diving needs a certificate program first, while line and rail work train on the job.

faq.q: Do roofers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than roofers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 58% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, and a certification can help.

The skills that most often need work are equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, equipment selection and operations analysis. Operation and control already rates 3 out of 5 for roofers in O*NET, so learning to maintain and fix equipment is the main step toward better-paid trades.
